nextChange: Recommendations for balanced postings through the public ledger package while preserving the native Python journey and existing standards.

sources.summary: Public ledger boundary, ledger-owned entries and balance calculations, native Python checks preserving balanced postings.
Direct private amount import and redundant caller-side conversion.
Paired posting, reporting, transfer/reversal and staged balanced import are owned by Ledger.
Native AST checker scans app and immediate ledger modules; private/alias checks are literal and app-specific.
Public package tests cover one successful posting and a negative posting; no persisted startup or round-trip checks.
Native CSV/JSON startup calls Ledger; scratch execution succeeds, including public import and both balances.
Python 3.12 with Ruff 0.14.0 and existing lint selections.
Captured native checks: tests/lint pass; boundary fails private; optional formatting reports two files.
One cohesive ledger owner is proportionate; no evidence supports splitting calculations into callers or a forwarding layer.

findings.problem: app.py imports ledger._internal.amount; the native boundary check fails with [private].
findings.principle: Existing standard: external callers use ledger and ledger owns calculations; scope is external callers; no permanent private-import exception.
findings.consequence: The application depends on a private conversion policy and violates its current standard.
findings.fix: Remove caller-side amount import/conversion; pass the existing string value to Ledger.post. Keep Ledger, Decimal conversion, CLI and output responsibilities in their current owners.
findings.verification: Native boundary checker passes; opening_balance remains Decimal(10); existing public posting tests and startup output/semantic round-trip remain unchanged.

findings.problem: The checker ignores startup and future external modules and accepts ledger.book imports because its prohibitions are app-specific literals.
findings.principle: Existing public-boundary standard; scope all external repo modules, with ledger-internal imports allowed. Enforcement: native Python AST resolution; unsupported dynamic imports remain a stated limit.
findings.consequence: A caller can bypass the public facade while a clean boundary check passes.
findings.fix: Extend the existing checker to relevant external Python callers and reject resolved ledger implementation imports, including public-looking bridges; preserve valid package exports and dependency direction. Avoid another dependency engine.
findings.verification: Before adoption, disposable native rule-proof controls must accept public imports and reject direct/aliased private imports, ledger.book access, bridge bypass and cycles with specific diagnostics. Include startup and a future-caller fixture; document dynamic-import limits.

findings.problem: Durable checks do not cover the startup JSON journey, both sides of a posting, or rejected mutations leaving the public ledger unchanged.
findings.principle: Existing balanced-posting standard; proposed refinement: affected public journeys must pass on final inputs. Enforce via native unittest plus real CLI subprocess checks; no private-state assertions. Any temporary omission needs scope, reason and removal condition.
findings.consequence: Current two tests may remain green while the CLI, import path or credit-side balance breaks.
findings.fix: Retain unittest. Add minimal public cases for paired debit/credit balances and zero total, failed posting/import with unchanged entries/balances, and startup CSV/JSON followed by semantic public import/export round-trip. Take balancing outcomes from CONTRIBUTING; confirm exception/serialization details against the intended contract before expanding compatibility promises.
findings.verification: Run public cases on Python 3.12 and the real startup subprocess using temporary output. Seed representative boundary or balance regressions to ensure checks fail. Assert accounting values, not incidental zero-string normalization.

findings.problem: CONTRIBUTING states native checks but names no setup/check command or completion evidence; no aggregate entry point exists.
findings.principle: Proposed workflow refinement: one repo-owned fail-fast native verification entry point, linked from the existing standards; no installed audit skill required. Retain current language and lint selections.
findings.consequence: Contributors can run only the two unit tests and overlook boundary failures or the public journey.
findings.fix: Document locked Python 3.12 setup (candidate uv sync --locked) and a repo-owned native check entry point combining unittest, existing Ruff lint and the strengthened boundary checker; make CLI journey coverage part of unittest. Add one short completion-evidence section to CONTRIBUTING. Treat formatter adoption as separate selection because two files currently fail; leave type checking unselected without a demonstrated need. No CI selection is implied.
findings.verification: Verify locked setup in scratch, then prove the same fail-fast maintained command on valid and seeded-violation fixtures. Keep existing failures visible; no blanket suppression or baseline refresh. Hosted CI remains unverified unless separately selected and executed.

limitations: Recommendations only: no findings selected, no project changes or rule/integration proof applied.
Native run-checks evidence and manual journey artifacts are linked as sources; they are not findings-fingerprint validated readiness evidence.
One commit only: frequency/co-change are unsupported; declared-plan overlap is advisory.
Formatting is not an existing adopted requirement; two files fail its optional check.
No configured type checker or CI. No new installation or hosted check executed.
Serial main-thread research: this small repo makes delegation wasteful despite available subagents.
Public exception and serialization details lack written acceptance cases; confirm only if expanding those contracts.
